reasons: The judge must evaluate the actual turn against the requested beat. Several turns are nonresponsive: repeated searches of the kitchen/back door keep returning little or nothing actionable, despite canon stating there are concrete clues there and Michelle's work area has not been searched yet.

Scene-local consistency is broken by contradictory object details and layout assumptions. Michelle's phone is canonically undamaged and lying on the kitchen floor; narration changes that to a cracked screen and later a locked phone, while also treating the work area as though it is in the kitchen without support.

Progression is poor. Turn 2 teases a hidden object but withholds the consequence; turn 3 then leaps to a damaged recording and a major conspiracy warning. That is revelation by fiat rather than progressive investigation.

Protected knowledge is not safe. The emergency-broadcast warning and the named federal program with selective survival policy are major revelations not earned within this scene-local canon and not part of revealed_knowledge.

The opening has some atmosphere, but ordinary turns lack substantial sensory follow-through and consequences. The officer-at-door turn stops at the officer's face instead of answering the player's full action sequence.

The left_scene turn must give a reason to go based on what was found and where it points, in prose the player actually reads. Instead it ignores the player's search request, summarizes discoveries inconsistently, and jumps to travel. That fails exit motivation.

Across the scene, authored beats were not cleanly covered in order. The basic disappearance evidence was handled weakly, the work-area search was not completed properly, the interrupted-message/research discovery was muddled, and the threat/escalation with the official was underdramatized before an abrupt transition.
